subject: Order Form: SLA uptime thresholds & response window rebalance
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@summitretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Dorn <jane.dorn@summitretail.com>, procurement@summitretail.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — SLA items for discussion

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the draft order form. Our procurement and ops teams reviewed the SLA section and have a couple of asks that are blockers for internal approval. Summary of Summit Retail's proposed changes:

- Uptime target: change regional uptime guarantee from 99.95% to 99.90% for non-production (staging) environments; keep 99.95% for production critical paths.
- Service credit cap: cap monthly service credits at 25% of monthly invoice (we'd like to avoid unlimited exposure).
- Response times: tighten P1 response to 30 minutes for production incidents (instead of 60), leave P2 at 4 hours.
- Maintenance windows: allow a 6-hour monthly maintenance window per region with advanced 72-hour notice; allow a "rolling maintenance" clause outside peak hours rather than a single blackout day.

I attached a redline of the SLA section (OrderForm_SLA_redlines_v3.docx) that highlights our suggested language. We can be flexible on the credit math if the uptime threshold change is acceptable — Summit is trying to balance cost predictability with operational risk.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 99.90% staging / 99.95% production split and the 25% monthly credit cap? If you need to loop in legal, please do so; we need a response to Procurement by next Tuesday (2026-08-18) to keep our renewal timeline.

Appreciate it,
Ethan

--
Ethan Cole
Senior Procurement Manager | Summit Retail, Inc.
ethan.cole@summitretail.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@summitretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — SLA items for discussion

Ethan — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Laura (legal) and Ben (ops/pricing) to give us a quick read. High-level response: we are open to a regional split for staging vs production uptime; the biggest negotiation points will be the service-credit cap and the P1 response SLA.

A few quick clarifications from us while legal reviews the doc:
- When you say "non-production/staging" — can you confirm which hostnames or accounts will be designated per the order form? We prefer explicit environment mapping to avoid disputes about which requests are covered.
- For the service credit cap: Redwood normally caps at 50% monthly invoice for enterprise customers; 25% is aggressive but not impossible depending on the uptime bucketing and verification method (we prefer to use our telemetry and a joint-runbook for outage validation).
- Maintenance: a 6-hour monthly window with 72-hour notice is acceptable, but we will ask for a clause that allows emergency maintenance with immediate notice for security patches (these would be excluded from credits if reasonably required).

Laura / Ben — can you take a look at the attached redline and call out any legal/ops no-gos? If we can agree to the 99.90/99.95 split and 25% cap, Ben, please run a quick unit-cost impact so I can share with Ethan.

Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: OrderForm_SLA_redlines_v3.docx — legal read and proposed language

Markus / Ben — I reviewed the redlines and drafted replacement language for the most sensitive clauses. Key points:

1) Uptime split (staging vs production)
I added a definition section to the order form excerpt that explicitly maps "Production Environment" to the environment names and hostnames listed in Exhibit A. "Non-Production Environment" is defined to exclude any customer-facing endpoints identified in the same exhibit. This removes ambiguity and gives Summit the split requested without changing the measurement approach.

2) Service credit cap
Redwood's standard enterprise cap is 50% of monthly fees as a running cap across incidents. I proposed a compromise: 35% monthly cap plus an annual aggregate cap of 200% of monthly fees (so credits don't compound indefinitely across months). This addresses Summit's predictability concerns while protecting Redwood from runaway credits during an extended outage.

3) P1 response time
Legal is OK with the 30-minute target provided we add the following qualification: "Response means acknowledgement and initiation of remediation; resolution SLA remains dependent on incident complexity and is not guaranteed." I added tailored language to prevent a hard contractual obligation to resolve within an absolute time.

4) Maintenance windows and emergency patches
I inserted an explicit exclusion for emergency security patches, and added a clause requiring Redwood to provide post-maintenance incident reports for any maintenance that impacts availability beyond scheduled windows.

I've attached the doc with tracked-changes (OrderForm_SLA_redlines_v3_LB.docx) and extracted the revised clauses into a short redline snippet for faster review.

Action items:
- Markus: confirm whether the 35%/200% cap compromise is acceptable to Summit.
- Ben: run the cost model on the 35% cap and the 99.95 production SLO to estimate potential maximum exposure.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@summitretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Dorn <jane.dorn@summitretail.com>, procurement@summitretail.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — SLA items for discussion

Markus / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested language. Summit has discussed internally: we can accept the proposed split (explicit environment mapping in Exhibit A) and the security-patch exclusion. On the credit cap, 35% monthly with a 200% annual aggregate is an improvement over 50% and should be workable for Procurement.

Two final asks before we push to legal signature:

1) Please include the definition of "acknowledgement" for P1s (what counts as initiation of remediation) — a quick bullet list in the SLA will be fine (pager contact, incident ticket creation, triage call within target window).

2) Confirm telemetry and verification: Summit would like Redwood to include a link to the joint-runbook telemetry dashboard and agree to a 10-business-day dispute window after incident reports are issued.

If Redwood can confirm those two items in writing, Summit Procurement will mark this as "approved subject to DocuSign" and we can execute by end of week.

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic approach.
Ethan

--
